然而让这类时钟运转并非易事，驱动这些狭窄的核跃迁需要带宽极小的极高稳定激光器。

sentences.text: 从技术机制看，核时钟把计时参考从原子外层电子跃迁转向原子核内部的跃迁，这条路径的可行性取决于能否用激光稳定地激发那条极窄的核跃迁谱线。
上述限制意味着，本次结果的成立条件包含激光带宽与连续比对能力这两项工程条件；若脱离这些条件，核时钟相对原子钟的潜在优势未必能自动兑现。

sentences.text: 尚不清楚本次核时钟的稳定度与不确定度能否在更长连续运行中保持，也不清楚其与原子钟比对时是否已排除所有主要系统效应。

events.title: Nuclear clocks finally see the light
events.originalTitle: Nuclear clocks finally see the light
events.excerpt: The new nuclear clocks represent the culmination of more than 20 years of research and could become vital tools in precision tests of fundamental physics. Getting such clocks to work, however, proved no easy feat, because driving these narrow nuclear transitions requires highly stable lasers with extremely small bandwidths. Writing in Nature , they describe realizing working nuclear clocks based on transitions in nuclei of thorium-229. They thus created stabilized nuclear clocks that they could compare continuously to frequency standards derived from atomic clocks.

evidenceRecords.text: The new nuclear clocks represent the culmination of more than 20 years of research and could become vital tools in precision tests of fundamental physics.
Getting such clocks to work, however, proved no easy feat, because driving these narrow nuclear transitions requires highly stable lasers with extremely small bandwidths.
Writing in Nature , they describe realizing working nuclear clocks based on transitions in nuclei of thorium-229.
They thus created stabilized nuclear clocks that they could compare continuously to frequency standards derived from atomic clocks.
Their results set limits on how dark matter can couple to photons and the strong nuclear force that are comparable to those derived from today’s best atomic clocks.

He is also interested in creating a trapped-ion thorium nuclear clock that would be more isolated from its environment and could re-use many of the quantum control techniques developed for atomic and ion clocks.
Victor Flambaum , a theorist from the University of New South Wales, Australia who was not involved in either project, calls the teams’ devices the “first prototypes of nuclear clocks”.

events.title: How The Groundwork For F-47 Flight Testing Is Being Laid
events.originalTitle: How The Groundwork For F-47 Flight Testing Is Being Laid
events.excerpt: The testing plan for the U.S. Air Force’s sixth-generation F-47 fighter is continuing to take shape ahead of the type’s expected first flight in 2028. Mark Massaro, head of the AFTC, was asked about how the groundwork is being laid for F-47 testing during a virtual talk the Air & Space Forces Association’s Mitchell Institute for Aerospace Studies hosted yesterday.

evidenceRecords.text: The testing plan for the U.S.
Air Force’s sixth-generation F-47 fighter is continuing to take shape ahead of the type’s expected first flight in 2028.

Mark Massaro, head of the AFTC, was asked about how the groundwork is being laid for F-47 testing during a virtual talk the Air & Space Forces Association’s Mitchell Institute for Aerospace Studies hosted yesterday.

“So, I’ll leave timelines to the [F-47] program office and other folks to talk to, but what I will tell you are some of the things that we’re doing to accelerate our test capabilities to get critical capabilities out the door,” Massaro explained.
“Integrated test is a key component.” A rendering of the F-47 fighter.

events.title: EOS unveils next-generation Slinger C-UAS system
events.originalTitle: EOS unveils next-generation Slinger C-UAS system
events.excerpt: EOS Defense Systems USA has unveiled plans for a next-generation version of its Slinger counter-uncrewed aircraft system (C-UAS) remote weapon system, with US production scheduled to begin at the company’s Huntsville, Alabama facility in 2027. The upgraded Slinger is in the final stages of development and will introduce enhanced sensing and autonomous kill-chain capabilities. EOS said selectable autonomy will allow the system to respond to drone threats at a faster decision cycle, while retaining the current Slinger’s stabilised capability to engage targets while on the move.

evidenceRecords.text: EOS Defense Systems USA has unveiled plans for a next-generation version of its Slinger counter-uncrewed aircraft system (C-UAS) remote weapon system, with US production scheduled to begin at the company’s Huntsville, Alabama facility in 2027.

EOS said selectable autonomy will allow the system to respond to drone threats at a faster decision cycle, while retaining the current Slinger’s stabilised capability to engage targets while on the move.

The announcement follows an interview at Land Forces 2026 in which EOS Defence Systems Australia Executive Vice President Lee Kormany discussed the development of the Slinger for counter-drone applications, alongside the company’s EOS Interceptor and its involvement with the Leidos team on LAND 156.
EOS said further details on the next-generation Slinger and its US production plans will be released in the coming months.
The post EOS unveils next-generation Slinger C-UAS system first appeared on Unmanned airspace .
The upgraded Slinger is in the final stages of development and will introduce enhanced sensing and autonomous kill-chain capabilities.
